items.basis: The candidate claims the basin's existing settling volume finishes separation of particles above 100 microns, but biological growth (explicitly cited as a root cause) is not a dense mineral scale particle and cannot be centrifuged or settled by gravity; the mechanism addresses only one of the two stated failure drivers. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "progressive nozzle clogging from scale particles and biological growth in the recirculated water" versus RECORD "centrifuges scale particles above 100 microns out of the loop continuously"

The candidate declares "13-15 bar supply untouched" as a boundary condition, yet installing a hydrocyclone with an underflow collection pot on the return line introduces a permanent pressure drop that reduces the net head available to the recirculation pump, indirectly altering supply hydraulics unless pump curves are re-matched. GROUNDED_IN: SCOPE "13-15 bar supply untouched" versus RECORD "one 150 mm hydrocyclone on the return line"

No internal numerical or logical contradiction exists within the candidate's own claims. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "loop particle concentration above 100 microns falls 85 percent" is internally consistent with RECORD "scale-driven clogging events fall from 4.1 to approximately 2.6"

Because the mechanism exclusively targets scale particles above 100 microns and ignores biological growth, the residual clogging rate may remain equivalent to baseline for bio-fouling events, preventing the system from reliably beating the un-invented standard across all failure modes. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "progressive nozzle clogging from scale particles and biological growth" versus RECORD "centrifuges scale particles above 100 microns"

Backflushing the automated underflow collection pot to a scale skip at each roll change requires interrupting the continuous return-line flow or valving around the cyclone during operation, which is not specified and threatens the claim of continuous decay. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "backflushed to a scale skip at each roll change" versus RECORD "centrifuges scale particles above 100 microns out of the loop continuously"

The testable prediction specifies isokinetic counts on the return and basin-outlet lines to prove 85 percent removal, but the basin-outlet is upstream of the supply header and downstream of the return line; measuring there conflates the cyclone's performance with the basin's pre-existing settling, making it physically impossible to isolate the cyclone's specific 85 percent removal claim using the stated measurement points. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "isokinetic particle counts on return and basin-outlet lines show 85 percent plus or minus 5 percent removal above 100 microns" versus RECORD "the basin'
